dervis-irab:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(إِذا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزالَها) (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, attached to (تحدث), which is the apodosis; the clause (زلزلت) is in the position of genitive through the annexation of the adverb to it. (زلزلت) is a passive past verb, (الأرض) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and (زلزالها) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being a maṣdar annexed to its agent; the meaning is "its quaking that it deserves and that its mass and greatness demand". It is also said that (إذا) is merely for time-reference and its governing element is omitted, i.e., "they will be gathered"; and it is said that the implied governor is "remember!", so that it is a direct object. The common reading is with kasra on the zāy, and it was also read with fatḥa; it is said that they are two maṣdars of one meaning, and it is said that the maṣdar is the kasra form and the noun is the fatḥa form. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was read with kasra and with fatḥa on the zāy; the kasra form is a maṣdar and the fatḥa form is a noun. There is no pattern fa'lāl with fatḥa except in the reduplicated verbs." This holds for the most part; otherwise there is "nāqa khazʿāl". In al-Qāmūs: "Khazʿala: the hyena limped and was lame; the walker shook his legs; and a she-camel with khazʿāl: lame. There is no fa'lāl from a non-reduplicated root other than it, and qusṭāl and khurṭāl." It also has: "zalzalahu zalzalatan and zilzālan and zalzālan (with three vowelings): he shook it; and al-zalāzil are calamities." Ibn ʿArafa said: al-zalzala and al-taltala are the same, and al-zalāzil and al-talātil; and he recited the verse of al-Rāʿī:
فأبوك سيدها وأنت أشدّها ... زمن الزلازل في التلاتل جولا
(Your father was their chief, and you are the strongest of them in the time of quakings, in the tremors, when they roamed [in confusion].) [Translator's note: the last word of the verse is rendered as it stands; the verse is obscure.]
(وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقالَها) Conjoined to what precedes. (أخرجت) is a past verb, (الأرض) its fāʿil, and (أثقالها) its direct object; the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun for added emphasis and to magnify the terror of the Hour. (أثقالها) is a direct object and is the plural of thiql with kasra, like ḥiml and aḥmāl, as in al-Mukhtār. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: "He made what lies within it of buried things its burdens." (وَقالَ الْإِنْسانُ: ما لَها) The wāw is a conjunction; (قال الإنسان) is verb and fāʿil; (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ and (لها) is its khabar. Regarding (الإنسان) there are two views: one, that it is a generic noun that includes the believer and the unbeliever, i.e., all of them will say that, because of the dreadful matter that overwhelms them, as they will say, "Who has raised us from our resting place?"; and the second, that it is the unbeliever in particular, because he did not believe in the resurrection, whereas the believer says, "This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth." (يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبارَها) (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, in the position of accusative as a badal from (إذا), and its governing element is the governing element of the thing replaced. The tanwīn is a compensation for a clause, i.e., "the day when the earth is shaken with its quaking, and the earth brings out its burdens, and man says, What is the matter with it?"; these three clauses were omitted and the tanwīn took their place, so two sukūns met, the dhāl and the tanwīn, and the dhāl was given kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns. This kasra on the dhāl is not a kasra of case-ending even though (إذ) is in the position of genitive through the annexation of what precedes it to it; the kasra is only for the meeting of two sukūns. This tanwīn is called tanwīn al-ʿiwaḍ (compensatory tanwīn).
(تحدث) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "she", i.e., the earth; the first object of (تحدث) is omitted, i.e., "creation". (بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحى لَها) The bāʾ is a preposition; (أن) and what is within its scope are in the position of genitive through the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تحدث). The meaning is: she reports her news on account of your Lord's revelation to her and His command to her to report. (أن) and its noun, and the clause (أوحى) is its khabar; (لها) are two elements attached to (أوحى), the lām meaning "to" (ilā); it was preferred over ilā in order to observe the rhyme-endings (fawāṣil); what takes ilā may take the lām, but not the reverse. (يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ أَشْتاتاً لِيُرَوْا أَعْمالَهُمْ) (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, a badal from the preceding (يومئذ), or attached to (يصدر), or an object of an implied "remember". (يصدر الناس) is imperfect verb and fāʿil; (أشتاتا) is a ḥāl from (الناس), plural of shatt, meaning scattered. One says amr shatt and shatāt, meaning dispersed and separate; it is a description by maṣdar. One says jāʾū ashtātan and jāʾū shatāta shatāta, meaning separately; the accusative is as ḥāl. ʿAdī ibn Zayd said:
قد هراق الماء في أجوافها ... وتطايرن بأشتات شقق
(The water had been poured out within their bellies, and they flew off in scattered, split-up pieces.) [Translator's note: the rendering of the verse is tentative.]
(ليروا): the lām is causal; (يروا) is a passive imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied (أن) after the lām; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; (أعمالهم) is a second direct object. The seeing is of the eye, which is why it is made to take two objects, since (أرى) takes three. The causal lām and what follows it are attached to (يصدر). (فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of consequence. (من) is a conditional noun that jusses, a mubtadaʾ; (يعمل) is the protasis and its fāʿil is a pronoun referring to (من); (مثقال ذرة) is a direct object; (خيرا) is a tamyīz or a badal from (مثقال); (يره) is the apodosis, jussive, its sign of jussive being the omission of the weak letter; and the hāʾ is the object of (ير). The protasis and apodosis together are the khabar of (من). The second sentence is conjoined to the first and its parsing is like its parsing. In Ibn Khālawayh: "The grandfather of al-Farazdaq came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, let me hear something of what Allah sent down to you.' He recited to him (إذا زلزلت); when he reached His saying (فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة) etc., he said: 'Enough for me, O Messenger of Allah.' And Abū ʿAbd Allāh related to me from Abū l-ʿAynāʾ from al-Aṣmaʿī, who said: A Bedouin recited (فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره), putting the words in reverse order, so I said to him, 'You have advanced and delayed,' and he said:
خذا جنب هرشى أو قفاها فإنه ... كلا جانبي هرشى لهنّ طريق
(Take the side of Harshā or its back, for both sides of Harshā are a road for them [the camels].)"
Al-Zamakhsharī also relates this anecdote in his Kashshāf and adds: "Al-dharra is the small ant; and it is said that al-dharr is the specks seen in the sunbeam." Harshā (like sukrā) is a mountain pass on the road to Mecca near al-Juḥfa. The meaning: take the front of that pass or behind it, for the situation is that both of its sides are a road for the camels you are seeking. The repetition of the word Harshā is to fix it in the hearer's mind for fear of heedlessness of it; the occasion was an occasion of guidance, so that was fitting.
